  Our Uruguay VIP selection includes a major South American journey featuring a day trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. This is a 26-day itinerary through Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Chile, not a separate multi-day holiday in Uruguay. We explain the Uruguay day, confirmed services and how to choose a different route if you want to spend more time in the country discovering Colonia del Sacramento, wineries or the Atlantic coast.
---

## VIP tours of Uruguay: what does the catalog actually offer?

Our VIP selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting [Uruguay](/uruguay/). The main distinction when choosing is between **the time spent in Uruguay and the duration of the entire journey**. On the current itinerary, most of the trip takes place in Argentina and Patagonia, with visits to Brazil and Chile; one day is allocated to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/).

This is a convenient way to see Uruguay's capital while keeping Argentina at the center of your journey. If you want several days on the Atlantic coast or an in-depth visit to Uruguay's historic towns, this particular itinerary does not provide that on its own.

**Our VIP selection includes itineraries with different service arrangements.** It does not prove that every excursion is private, all hotels are five-star or every transfer is in a separate vehicle. The current itinerary explicitly includes a group tour of Montevideo with an English-speaking guide. This confirmed condition matters more than the general “VIP” designation.

## Which tour visits Uruguay?

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) includes Buenos Aires, Iguazu Falls, Salta and Cafayate, Mendoza's wine regions, the Bariloche lakes, glaciers near El Calafate, El Chalten, Ushuaia and Chile's Torres del Paine. One separate day is devoted to Montevideo.

| Detail | Confirmed by the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Overall duration | 26 days across several countries |
| Uruguay | One-day visit to Montevideo |
| Crossing | Return ferry trip included |
| Excursion | Group tour with English-speaking guide |
| End of the day | Return to Buenos Aires |

On day 3, after breakfast, travelers leave Buenos Aires for Montevideo. The sightseeing route passes through central districts, includes a stop at a market and continues to the waterfront. In the evening the itinerary calls for a return to Argentina.

The price of the entire 26-day journey covers accommodation in hotels, meals and excursions specified by the program; however, **international and domestic flights are listed among services not included**. The Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires ferry is included. The total price and conditions apply to the whole trip and must not be described as the cost of a one-day VIP tour of Uruguay.

## What can you see in Montevideo in one day?

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is Uruguay's capital and largest city. Its historic center, European-influenced streets, broad squares and long Rambla promenade offer a first impression of the country even on a short visit.

The tour begins at Independence Square and the monument to Jose Artigas. It then follows 18 de Julio Avenue towards the Parliament building. This is a busy overview of the city's history and layout, without a promise of entering every museum along the way.

The route also includes a market where visitors can see local produce and discover the city's food culture. The Prado district follows, with parks and rose gardens, a drive near Centenario Stadium, and the Carrasco and Punta Gorda neighborhoods. The tour concludes with views of the River Plate coast and the Rambla.

**This is an overview tour.** Mentioning a landmark on the route does not imply a lengthy visit to its interior or exhibits. If museums, particular restaurants or the architecture of one neighborhood are priorities, a single group day is too short.

## Why it is convenient to combine Montevideo and Buenos Aires

The cities stand on opposite shores of the River Plate estuary. A visit to Montevideo therefore fits naturally into a longer journey through [Argentina](/argentina/). A ferry crossing provides a chance to see another capital within the same journey and return to Buenos Aires in the evening.

This logistics arrangement also means that transport takes part of the day. Time actually spent at sightseeing stops is shorter than the overall duration of the excursion. On a 26-day itinerary, it makes sense as a separate outing between major Argentine stages. For an independent exploration of Uruguay, however, it is too brief.

Ferry schedules, documentation requirements, border procedures and excursion availability depend on the date and each traveler's nationality. Check these details for the actual departure. A blanket promise of unrestricted border crossing would be inaccurate.

If you want to visit more countries, explore the [combined itineraries catalog](/multi-country/). For an extensive stay within Uruguay itself, use the [country guide](/uruguay/) and [all tours featuring Uruguay](/uruguay/tour/), rather than relying solely on this VIP selection.

## Places worth seeing on a longer Uruguay itinerary

Uruguay has much more to offer than its capital. Yet **the following places are not included in the confirmed Uruguay day of the 26-day VIP tour**. Consider them only when choosing a separate program or making agreed changes to the itinerary.

### Colonia del Sacramento: history by the River Plate

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) is known for cobbled streets, low historic houses and views across the estuary. Founded by the Portuguese in 1680, it retains elements of both Portuguese and Spanish urban traditions. Its Historic Quarter joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1995.

Unlike a major capital, Colonia is easy to explore on foot. It appeals to travelers interested in colonial South American history. Its visit must not be treated as part of the Montevideo sightseeing trip merely because both cities are in Uruguay.

### Punta del Este: a separate beach-holiday format

[Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) is known for beaches, restaurants, sea views and resort life. Allow several days if you want to spend time on beaches, walking and traveling along the coast.

The warmest and busiest season on the Atlantic coast is the Southern Hemisphere summer, from December to February. Milder months can suit city walks, while swimming depends on the day's actual weather. Punta del Este is **a separate destination**, not a stop on the 26-day itinerary that includes Montevideo.

### Wineries and gastronomy

Uruguay has a distinct wine tradition, particularly associated with red wines made from Tannat grapes. Wineries can be found near the capital and in other areas. For example, [Bouza Winery](/uruguay/place/bouza-winery/) is an appealing option for travelers who want to combine tasting with a gastronomic day.

Wine estates are also a theme for a dedicated itinerary. But **a tasting at Bouza is not included in the current VIP tour through Montevideo**; adding it to the list of confirmed services would be incorrect.

## Choosing between a short visit and a dedicated Uruguay holiday

For travelers already planning an extended journey through Argentina, a one-day trip to Montevideo offers a good first encounter with Uruguay without arranging a separate holiday. You will see urban districts, historic sights, the waterfront and some of the neighboring country's culture.

For a more in-depth visit, the priorities differ: how many nights to spend in Montevideo, whether [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) interest you, whether to add a wine day and how to divide time between city and coast. This calls for a different allocation of days.

If VIP means a personal guide, private car or particular hotel category to you, compare the **actual confirmed service terms**. On the 26-day tour, the Uruguay day is group-based with an English-speaking guide. Describing it as a private VIP excursion would be incorrect.

## Frequently asked questions about VIP tours of Uruguay

### How many days does the current VIP tour spend in Uruguay?

On the [26-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Uruguay is visited for 1 day: a trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo and back to Argentina. The remaining days belong to the wider journey.

### Are the ferry and city tour included?

According to the selected itinerary, the Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires ferry and a group sightseeing excursion are included. An English-speaking guide conducts the tour.

### Can I see Colonia del Sacramento on this tour?

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) is absent from the Uruguay day's itinerary. You would need a different route or separately confirmed adjustment to visit it.

### Is Punta del Este included in the VIP journey?

No. On the current offer, the Uruguay stage is devoted to Montevideo. [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) is better considered as a separate seaside stay, with extra time for travel and relaxation.

### Do all VIP tours include a personal guide?

No. On this specific itinerary, the Montevideo excursion is expressly described as a group tour with an English-speaking guide. A private format must be confirmed in the chosen program's terms rather than assumed from the catalog name.

## Adventure VIP tours featuring Uruguay: where are the active stages?

**It is important here to distinguish the geography visited from the character of the whole journey.** Our selection currently includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: the [26-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), which also travels through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay. The Uruguay portion is a one-day visit to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Mountain trails, glaciers and the main adventure experiences are concentrated chiefly in Argentina and Chile.

This tour suits travelers who want to combine a major journey with a short introduction to Uruguay. Trekking through Uruguayan natural areas or several days of active recreation on its Atlantic coast would require a different itinerary. **A tour appearing simultaneously under VIP, Adventure and Uruguay does not mean that sporting activities take place specifically in Uruguay.**

## What the Uruguay day actually includes

On day three of the [26-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), travelers leave [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for Montevideo and return the same day. **A group excursion with an English-speaking guide and ferry tickets** are included. Since the day starts and ends in Argentina's capital, it is a brief visit to Uruguay rather than a separate multi-day stage.

In Montevideo, the route passes Independence Square, 18 de Julio Avenue, the Prado area, Carrasco, Punta Gorda and the Rambla waterfront. It includes city sightseeing stops, a market and an introduction to local food. This is a sightseeing day with transfers, not a trekking, safari or sports expedition.

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is appealing for its mixture of historic quarters, open coastal spaces and parks. If you enjoy walking, the Rambla offers a long waterfront promenade, while the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) is ideal for exploring architecture on foot. But an independent waterfront walk, like a bicycle tour, **is not confirmed as a separate included service** on the featured journey.

## Where the adventures really begin

The active experiences on the [larger itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) are spread across very different regions. In the northeast, you visit Iguazu Falls, including the [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The route later takes in Argentina's wine-growing northwest, high-altitude landscapes, the lake district and Patagonia.

Near [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), travelers encounter glacier scenery, including [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). [El Chalten](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) is associated with mountain trails and views across Patagonia. Another part of the journey passes through Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), while the southern section reaches [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/).

| Part of the trip | Main experiences |
|---|---|
| [Uruguay](/uruguay/) | One day in Montevideo, city and waterfront |
| [Argentina](/argentina/) | Patagonia, glaciers, mountain walks |
| [Chile](/chile/) | Torres del Paine region |
| [Brazil](/brazil/) | Iguazu Falls and nature trails |

The adventure classification therefore reflects the entire 26-day journey. Uruguay is its geographical and cultural component. The overall tour length does not indicate how long active activities last in a particular country; you need to read each day's itinerary to assess the effort involved.

## If you want adventures within Uruguay

Uruguay can be explored in a very different way. Coastal routes and the natural areas of Rocha Department, home to the dunes and beaches of Cabo Polonio, are interesting options for a separate trip. The country's official tourism portal describes access to Cabo Polonio on foot and by special transport, as well as a walking route from Barra de Valizas. This is a completely different experience from a city tour of Montevideo.

Another possibility is spending more time on Uruguay's coast, combining walks with stops in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) and nearby resort areas. To combine nature with historical towns, consider [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/). Decide in advance which parts should be physically active and where you would rather leave time for relaxed walks.

**Cabo Polonio, Punta del Este and Colonia del Sacramento are not included in the Uruguay day of the featured 26-day tour.** They are ideas for arranging a longer stay within the country. They must not be attributed to the existing program simply because they are in Uruguay. The main nature and historical options appear in our [Uruguay travel guide](/uruguay/).

## Combining Uruguay with Argentina without unnecessary transfers

Buenos Aires and Montevideo lie on opposite sides of the River Plate estuary. On the current tour, transport is arranged by ferry in both directions; after visiting Montevideo, the journey continues through Argentina. This allows you to see Uruguay's capital without substantially altering a longer route.

For active recreation in Uruguay, however, one day is not enough. You would need to redistribute days, plan additional transfers and choose a specific natural area. Then compare not only the countries listed but also **overnight stays in Uruguay, exact activities, travel time and guiding arrangements**.

This matters particularly for a VIP request. A private active trip cannot be assumed from the catalog name: the current Montevideo outing is group-based with an English-speaking guide. Any different arrangements, including a private excursion, extra accommodation or vehicle, require separate confirmation.

## What to choose: extensive Patagonia or active Uruguay?

The [26-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) stands out for its broad geography: tropical Iguazu, northwestern Argentina, lake districts, glaciers and Tierra del Fuego. The day in Uruguay is an enjoyable cultural addition. It makes sense if Patagonia and several countries matter more to you than an in-depth visit to Uruguay.

If your journey should revolve around Uruguay's nature, outdoor activities and coast, start with the [general Uruguay tours catalog](/uruguay/tour/) and the [adventure selection featuring the country](/interests/adventure/tours/uruguay/). These sections may overlap with the VIP selection: they display real tours on the site, not a guarantee of a separate sports program in every country named.

To compare the full VIP segment, explore [VIP tours featuring Uruguay](/vip/uruguay/). Base your decision on the precise itinerary and discuss separately the days you want to spend in Uruguay itself.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a dedicated adventure VIP tour entirely within Uruguay?

The current selection features a [26-day multi-country journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) with a one-day visit to Montevideo. Its itinerary does not include an independent multi-day active stage within Uruguay.

### Are trekking or water sports included in Montevideo?

No such activities are listed for the Uruguay day. The confirmed services are a group city sightseeing tour and ferry tickets. Walks or bicycle outings along the Rambla are possible urban activities, but they are not included in the published package.

### Why is this tour considered adventurous?

Because the theme applies to the entire journey, which includes Patagonia, mountain regions, glacier landscapes and nature routes. It does not mean that every day or every country has the same level of active pursuits.

### Can the Montevideo visit be replaced with several days on the coast?

That would be a modification of the current itinerary. The length, transport, accommodation and activities would need to be agreed separately. The [Uruguay guide](/uruguay/) can help you decide which areas to include.

## Cultural and historical VIP tours featuring Uruguay: what is actually included?

**The key question when choosing this journey is how much time you will spend in Uruguay and which historic sites you will visit.** The country has several World Heritage landmarks, but appearing on a multi-country itinerary does not mean you will tour all of them.

Our VIP selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. One of its itineraries is [Argentina and Patagonia in 26 Days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/). The Uruguayan part takes place on day three: a ferry crossing from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and a return that same day. Ferry tickets are included, and an English-speaking guide leads the **group** excursion. The remaining days focus chiefly on Argentina, Patagonia, Iguazu and other parts of the route.

This is a significant distinction: **VIP is the name of a commercial website selection, not confirmation of a private guide and five-star hotels on every segment.** The format of the Montevideo excursion is explicitly stated on this particular tour.

## Montevideo: a city's history in one day

The streets and squares of [Montevideo's historic center](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) reveal how the capital developed on the shores of the River Plate. On the featured longer itinerary, sightseeing begins at [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/) and the monument to Jose Artigas. The route then follows 18 de Julio Avenue towards the Parliament building.

The itinerary also includes a market with local food, the Prado district with parks and historic mansions, Centenario Stadium, the Carrasco and Punta Gorda districts and the coastal Rambla. Thus one day combines national history, urban architecture and everyday life in the capital.

For a more in-depth independent visit, the [Cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/) and the old streets of the center are also worth exploring. **These additional sites must not automatically be assumed to be part of the 26-day tour's group excursion**; follow the exact list of scheduled stops.

Montevideo is a useful introduction to Uruguay's history. One sightseeing day provides an overview, but museums, unhurried walks and individual architectural landmarks require more time.

## Colonia del Sacramento: Portuguese and Spanish heritage

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) was founded by the Portuguese in 1680. Its historic quarter has been UNESCO World Heritage-listed since 1995. Unlike the regular grid of many Spanish colonial cities, the old town retains an irregular street pattern, cobbled lanes and buildings reflecting Portuguese and Spanish influences.

Colonia is a place for walking slowly through the historic quarter, examining its streets, walls, façades and relationship with the river, rather than simply checking another capital off a travel list.

**Colonia is not included in the one-day Uruguay portion of the 26-day itinerary.** It does appear on the [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) and the [4-day Wine and Old Believer Traditions itinerary](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/). These are separate products; compare their conditions and format independently from the VIP selection.

## Historical routes beyond the capital

Another part of Uruguayan history appears in [San Javier](/uruguay/place/san-javier/), a settlement associated with immigrants from the Russian Empire. On the 4-day tour, travelers arrive there after visiting Montevideo and the Spinoglio winery. The route then continues to [Fray Bentos](/uruguay/place/fray-bentos/), known for its industrial heritage.

The Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2015. It reveals another side of Uruguay: the history of production, labor and trade linked to international markets.

UNESCO also recognizes the Church of Atlantida, designed by engineer Eladio Dieste. But **mentioning a landmark in a travel guide does not mean that its visit is included in the tours listed here**.

Uruguay's candombe and tango traditions are also valuable for those interested in urban culture. They help explain the wider River Plate region, but attendance at a particular musical performance must be explicitly specified in the itinerary.

## Choosing a route by the depth of its cultural experiences

| Itinerary | Cultural portion in Uruguay |
|---|---|
| [26 days: Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) | One day in Montevideo; group excursion |
| [13 days: 3 countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) | Colonia, Montevideo and further stops in Uruguay |
| [4 days: wine and traditions](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) | Montevideo, San Javier, Fray Bentos, Colonia |
| [6 days: Best of Uruguay](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) | Private capital tour, Punta del Este and wineries |

If Uruguay is meant to be **a brief extension to a larger journey**, the ferry itinerary from Buenos Aires is convenient. If the country's own history is the main goal, a route including Colonia, San Javier and Fray Bentos is more appropriate. To combine architecture, good hotels and gastronomy, consider the separate six-day itinerary, which specifies accommodation arrangements and private excursions.

Explore both [all tours of Uruguay](/uruguay/tour/) and the [general Uruguay VIP catalog](/vip/uruguay/): these selections serve different purposes. Being listed in one does not itself change the included services.

## What to consider when planning

Crossing the River Plate requires coordinating the ferry and excursion schedule. That is already part of the sightseeing day on the 26-day trip, but extensive independent exploration of Montevideo is not. On another route, check how many nights you will spend in Uruguay, where transfers begin and end, and whether an accompanying guide is provided.

In Colonia's historic center, cobblestones and uneven surfaces matter. If a traveler needs accessible routes or shorter walking distances, discuss that when selecting the itinerary. Visits to wineries, museums and concerts must be checked against the actual services of the chosen tour.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Colonia del Sacramento included in the 26-day VIP tour?

No. The Uruguay portion of that journey is a one-day sightseeing tour of Montevideo. Colonia appears on other Ada Tours itineraries, including the [13-day three-country route](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/).

### Is the Montevideo excursion private?

On the 26-day journey, it is a group tour with an English-speaking guide. On the separate [six-day Uruguay tour](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/), the capital is visited on a private English-language excursion.

### Which historical sites in Uruguay are UNESCO World Heritage?

The list includes the Historic Quarter of Colonia del Sacramento, the Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape and Eladio Dieste's Church of Atlantida. Their UNESCO status does not mean all three are included in a single travel itinerary.

### Can Uruguay's culture be combined with wine?

Yes. The [4-day Old Believer traditions tour](/uruguay/tour/uruguay-wine-old-believer-traditions/) combines a winery, historic settlements and Colonia. To choose a wine-focused option, start with [gastronomic tours of Uruguay](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/).

### How much time should I allow to discover Uruguay?

A single excursion day can give you an overview of Montevideo. Colonia, historical routes in western Uruguay, wineries and the coast require extra days. Compare real stops and transfers in the itineraries, not just the total number of countries in their titles.

## Uruguayan Tannat: where to discover local winemaking

Tannat has become an internationally recognizable symbol of Uruguayan wine. Wine itineraries differ geographically: some can be conveniently combined with [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), while others require a separate trip to the country's west or Atlantic coast.

| Area | Main interest |
|---|---|
| [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) | Family estates, Tannat, tastings |
| Carmelo | Wine route and small wineries |
| Maldonado | Vineyards and coastline |

### Canelones: family wineries near the capital

[Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) is home to a substantial share of the country's wineries. The departmental tourism authority states that more than 60% of Uruguay's wineries are located here. Many welcome organized visits; their owners introduce grape growing, production and wine aging. Comparing grape varieties and interpretations of Tannat from different producers is particularly interesting.

Canelones suits travelers who want to add a wine day to a journey through [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). However, the specific estates and tastings must be agreed as a separate program. They are not included in the existing 26-day tour.

### Carmelo: a separate journey along a wine route

Carmelo, in western Uruguay, lends itself to a slower-paced wine trip. The Ruta del Vino de Carmelo association brings together seven wineries close to one another. They offer insights into family winemaking traditions, walks among vineyards and tastings. A visit can be combined with historic [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/).

Even if several wineries are nearby, each visit takes time. It is more practical to choose one or two estates and arrange your visit than to expect to see them all in a day. This is an idea for a separate itinerary, not a promise of a service already included by Ada Tours.

### Maldonado: wine and time by the ocean

Maldonado is appealing for its vineyards, rural landscapes and Atlantic coast. If you plan to spend time in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/), a winery excursion could be a separate part of the trip. When choosing an estate, the actual distance from your accommodation and availability of visits matter more than the general region name. Specific accommodation and transport here are not included in a ready-made gastronomic VIP offer.

## Where the tastings take place on the Ada Tours itinerary

The [26-day multi-country tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) details its wine program by Argentine region. At Cafayate, a winery and wine museum visit are scheduled. Later, from [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), travelers visit 3 wineries in Lujan Valley for tastings and lunch. The following wine day is devoted to Uco Valley, with 2 more winery visits.

The [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) day has different experiences: the historic center, Parliament, Prado district, market and Rambla. This city visit offers an introduction to Uruguay's cuisine and way of life, but **a Uruguayan winery and specialist Tannat tasting are absent from the day's itinerary**.

| Item | Confirmed itinerary |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | One day in Montevideo |
| Wineries | Argentina |
| Duration | 26 days |
| Excursion in Uruguay | Group tour, in English |

Ada Tours' VIP section lets you compare our offers. The label alone does not confirm a private vehicle, personal sommelier, wine dinner at a closed estate or particular hotel category. This tour's services are mixed and include group excursions. For exact terms, see [its program page](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/).

## Choosing a gastronomic itinerary

**If you want to combine Argentine wine with travel through 4 countries**, the [26-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) covers Argentina's wine regions, Uruguay, Iguazu, Patagonia and other stops. It is designed for an extensive trip, not for prolonged exploration of one wine-growing region.

## When to plan a wine trip

In the Southern Hemisphere, the warm months fall between December and March. Grape harvesting times depend on region, variety and weather, so visits during harvest must be arranged individually. Other seasons also offer interesting experiences: winery tours can explain production and aging, offer tastings and introduce local gastronomic traditions.

If several wineries are planned for one day, determine the order and transport in advance. Avoid driving yourself after tastings. For Carmelo and Canelones, confirming visitor hours for your chosen date is particularly useful: not every estate operates like a museum with unrestricted walk-in admission.

## Nature-focused VIP tours featuring Uruguay: where are the main excursions?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Uruguay is one of the principal countries on these itineraries, but **that does not mean every nature excursion takes place within Uruguay**. Some programs devote one city day to the country, while the most extensive natural stops are in Argentina, Brazil, Chile or elsewhere.

On the [26-day Argentina and Patagonia journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Uruguay is represented by a day trip from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), returning in the evening. Ferry tickets are included, and the tour is conducted in a group with an English-speaking guide. Nature experiences include [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the lakes around Bariloche, [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), El Chalten, Ushuaia and Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/).

The [20-day journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) takes in Rio, both sides of Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Montevideo, then continues to Atacama, Bolivia's [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and Inca heritage sites in Peru. It is appealing to travelers who want to contrast the tropical forest around the waterfalls with dry, high-altitude landscapes.

The [32-day eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) combines Iguazu and Montevideo with Atacama, Uyuni, Peru and the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Its confirmed terms specify 4-star hotels and domestic flights. Visiting many countries also means significant time in transit, so review the actual duration of each stop.

## Uruguay's own natural landscapes: ocean, dunes and lagoons

Uruguay differs from the humid Atlantic forests near Iguazu and the cold glaciers of Patagonia. Its landscape is dominated by low hills, grasslands, coastal plains and a long ocean shore. In [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), even a short tour offers views of the River Plate and the long Rambla promenade, but it remains primarily an urban visit.

For a dedicated nature journey, the coast east of [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) is particularly interesting. Cabo Polonio National Park in Rocha Department protects dunes, beaches, rocky headlands and offshore islands. Rocha Lagoon offers a different environment: shallow brackish water, coastal grasslands and waterbird habitats. These areas are described in Uruguay's official register of protected areas.

**A visit to Cabo Polonio or Rocha Lagoon is not automatically part of a nature-themed VIP tour that stops in Montevideo.** These are separate ideas for exploring the country. They can be discussed when arranging a private route, but access, overland transfers and season must be checked first.

For a relaxed coastal stop, consider [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/); [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) reveals the country's historical side. Cultural excursions and nature walks are best planned on separate days.

## Seasons, clothing and documents

A single journey may include warm, humid Iguazu, cold and windy Patagonia and the dry highlands of the Andes. These stops need different clothing: light rain protection at the falls, warm layers and a windproof jacket in the south, and sun protection at altitude. Discuss the effects of elevation and potential physical exertion before choosing a tour.

Choose the season based on the main nature excursions rather than Montevideo's climate. Rainfall and accessible trails matter at Iguazu; weather matters for glaciers; mountain regions require attention to temperature and road conditions. Check each national park's visiting rules for your dates before booking.

Crossing several borders requires checking visa, transit and medical-document rules for each traveler's nationality. We can help organize those checks and coordinate flights and ferries, but entry permits cannot be guaranteed.
